manager_rule: Detect Rule-46 + Rule-33-alone co-fire and defer the Rule-46 absorber bypass by one round (symmetric single-cable case, no Rule-50/51). After evaluating round R: if Rule 46 fires (all compiler stubs eliminated — n_stubs > 0 AND absorbed + trimmed_spurs == n_stubs AND kelvin_unrouted > 0, storing the compiler nets list as absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed per Rule 46's normal protocol) AND Rule 33 fires for exactly one cable index C_sym (both /SENSEC{C_sym}_HI and /SENSEC{C_sym}_LO appear in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines') in the same round R, AND Rule 50 does NOT fire for any cable in round R (no asymmetric single-member Kelvin failure exists — Rule 51 therefore cannot fire, and Rule 52 is not armed): (1) store the round-R compiler nets (e.g. {/CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA}) as a session-scoped set 'deferred_rule46_bypass_nets_r33_only'; (2) in round R+1, Rule 33's mandatory_kelvin_bypass proceeds as normal — Kelvin force stubs for C_sym are injected with full absorber-exempt status per Rule 34, and ALL compiler stubs are suppressed per Rule 34; Rule 46's absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed flag is cleared (it has nothing to operate on in R+1 because there are no compiler stubs); (3) in round R+2, if the compiler generates stubs for any net whose name is a member of deferred_rule46_bypass_nets_r33_only, pass those stubs through the absorber, spur-trimmer, and orphan-removal stages WITHOUT elimination for round R+2 only — exactly the bypass-pass-through semantics Rule 46 would have applied in R+1 had mandatory_kelvin_bypass not suppressed all compiler stubs; do NOT suppress net_absorption_count increments for round R+2 (the false-positive suppression already applied in R per Rule 46's normal protocol); compiler stubs for nets NOT in deferred_rule46_bypass_nets_r33_only in R+2 are processed normally; (4) reset deferred_rule46_bypass_nets_r33_only to empty immediately after round R+2 is dispatched, regardless of outcome; (5) log 'rule46_rule33_only_cofire_bypass_deferral' with fields: (a) round R, (b) C_sym and failing Kelvin member names, (c) nets stored in deferred_rule46_bypass_nets_r33_only, (d) confirmation that Rule 50 did not fire in round R and therefore Rule 51/52 are not armed, (e) confirmation that R+1 applies mandatory_kelvin_bypass per Rule 34 suppressing all compiler stubs, (f) confirmation that R+2 will apply the deferred bypass for stored nets, (g) net_absorption_count values for the stored nets at time of storage. This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 46, 52, and 53; it does not modify net_absorption_count (Rule 46's round-R suppression still applies), compiler_excluded_nets, consecutive_rule46_suppression_count, or any other session-scoped state maintained by those rules, and does not replace or defer any action they independently mandate. It is explicitly subordinate to Rule 52 and Rule 53: if Rule 51 DOES fire (Rule 52 is armed), Rule 52/53 govern instead of this rule. Rationale: Rule 52 was authored to handle Rule-46 + Rule-51 co-fire, where Rule 51's mandatory_kelvin_bypass voids Rule 46's bypass intent in R+1. The identical voiding mechanism occurs in the simpler case where only Rule 33 fires (symmetric single-cable failure, no Rule-50 asymmetric co-fire) — Rule 34 suppresses all compiler stubs in R+1 regardless of whether the mandatory_kelvin_bypass originates from Rule 33 alone or Rule 51. Round 100 demonstrates the gap directly: cable-1 symmetric failure (Rule 33), all 7 compiler stubs for /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA absorbed (Rule 46 fires), cable 2 fully routed (Rule 50 absent, Rule 51 absent, Rule 52 not armed) — Rule 46's bypass for those signal nets will be silently voided by round 101's mandatory_kelvin_bypass with no recovery path. Deferring one round to R+2 (the first round without a mandatory_kelvin_bypass from R's Rule 33) preserves Rule 46's false-positive-prevention intent across the suppression window.
